notes: High overlap (9/10 claims on child mortality improvements). LLM marks UNCERTAIN due to lack of causal evidence linking UN Summit to outcomes. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the interpretation that child mortality improvements drove life expectancy gains, viewing it as consistent with established knowledge.

Strong overlap (11/14 claims on HIV/smoking analysis). LLM finds covariate analysis well-documented and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, stating HIV/smoking 'not incorporated systematically' and may be 'proxy variables' requiring more comprehensive modeling of mortality causes.

Moderate overlap (6/23 claims on MM model justification). LLM finds conceptual application well-justified and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, questioning mechanistic analogy ('In what way is national wealth converted...by an enzyme') and stating model 'needs to be better justified' with no clear superiority over alternatives.

Moderate overlap (4/8 claims on adult survival crossover findings). LLM finds crossover analysis robustly documented and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN as these findings depend on critical income parameter validity, which they question.

Moderate overlap (5/11 claims on adult survival reversal). LLM finds 'reversal of fortune' well-documented and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting 'income alone does not adequately explain these changes' and emphasizing oversimplification of 'complex interactions.'

Both agree logistic model's negative inflection points are problematic (C23-C25). LLM finds this strengthens case for MM model. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding, focusing critique on why MM should be preferred over other alternatives.

Both accept empirical findings on maximum life expectancy trends (C28-C30). LLM finds strong statistical fits. Peer reviewers do not challenge these descriptive temporal trends, suggesting implicit acceptance.

Both agree on limitations regarding cause-specific mortality data (C104-C106). LLM acknowledges <3% of child deaths certified. Peer reviewers support need for better data through their critique that analysis should 'incorporate them all' if data existed.

Partial overlap (4/12 claims on child vs adult divergence). LLM finds divergence clearly demonstrated and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN due to concerns about critical income parameter robustness ('virtually all data points above it'), casting doubt on precise quantitative estimates.

Both mark UNCERTAIN for future projections and policy recommendations (C73-C75). LLM notes these are 'speculative extrapolations' not empirically tested. Peer reviewers question interpretation through methodological concerns about model justification.

Both accept historical claims about MM equation applications (C85-C89). These are well-established facts about the model's use in other domains. Peer reviewers' concerns focus on this particular application, not historical precedents.

Overlap on policy recommendations (C83, C115-C116). LLM marks UNCERTAIN as these represent future work not demonstrated results. Peer reviewers SUPPORT policy implications about available interventions, consistent with their acknowledgment of changing risk factors.

Both address sensitivity analysis (C26-C27). LLM finds robustness to 5% data removal SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting more extensive sensitivity exploration by 'removing certain data points,' suggesting reported analysis insufficient.

Overlap on critical income parameter definition (C16, C18-C20). LLM finds parameter 'mathematically sound and interpretable.' Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, calling it 'problematic' because 'virtually all data points are above it' and questioning robustness.

Minimal overlap (C21-C22) on model comparison. LLM finds comparable fit across models SUPPORTED, with MM advantage in interpretability. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting MM 'appears to fit just as well (or badly) as log-linear' without statistical justification for superiority.

Minimal overlap (C90, C96) on model limitations acknowledgment. LLM finds authors' honest assessment of limitations SUPPORTED and strengthening. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, viewing these same limitations as requiring better justification before acceptance.

Both accept basic divergence pattern between children and adults (C3, C35). LLM finds temporal pattern empirically documented. Peer reviewers do not challenge this finding, though they question precise parameter estimates through methodological concerns.

Minimal overlap (C5, C39-C40) on adult critical income increases. LLM finds increases robustly documented. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN due to broader concerns about critical income parameter robustness affecting all derivative findings.

Minimal overlap (C31, C34) on overall life expectancy findings. LLM finds empirical findings well-documented with strong statistical fits. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN about critical income parameter interpretability and robustness.
